last_attempts_log.asr_text: You get on the train and find a seat. At last, you can relax. Or so you think. Then you hear sounds from a video somewhere—laughter, sound effects, and cheerful music in the background. You are quietly going home, but your ears have to log into someone else's video suggestions. You paid for a train ticket, but you don't remember paying to see this show. One smartphone makes the whole train carriage an audience. That's a pretty bold show. Here's news about this kind of sound no one asks for. On October 19th, 2026, the UK announced the start of a national campaign. It asks train passengers to use headphones. But don't quickly think, in the UK, no headphones means you're breaking the law. No new rule bans all sound. The campaign points to current rail rules and asks people to think about others.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: Current rail rules ban sounds from a device when they bother other people. They may cover sound from a phone speaker, too, if the situation fits the rules. There is an exception when the train company has given written permission. A song may sound like a masterpiece to you, but not to the person beside you. If you break the rules, you could get a fine of up to £1,000. That's enough to make you reach for your wallet before the volume button. But remember the words "up to" and "could." It doesn't mean everyone who plays sound on a speaker gets a £1,000 fine. So the first step is a call to use headphones. People will see the message on posters and hear it in announcements at stations and on trains. The fine may be what people hear most, but let's hear the campaign's message, too.
